The Graduate Certificate in Natural Resources and the Environment was first online program proposed in CELS.
Our proposal included the creation of 6 required 2-credit courses (EVS 509, EVS 511, EVS 514, EVS 515, EVS 518 and EVS 519) that all enrolled students would complete to obtain the certificate.
Since the approval of both the courses and the program, URI Online has grown and developed more standard practices, including offering most accelerated online courses for 3 credits.

In order to be consistent with this format we are proposing to increase the credits for four of the courses from two to three and eliminate two other courses.
The workload in the remaining classes will be increased to reflect the additional credit by a combination of 1) additional readings and/or instructional videos to cover more content, 2) increasing the number of quizzes, discussion forums, and homework assignments, and 3) the addition or expansion of a final project.
Content will be redistributed over the remaining four courses, so all program learning outcomes will still be met.
The total number of required credits will remain the same (12).
The benefits of this restructuring extend to both students in the program as well as URI Online overall.
First, students will be able to complete the certificate in nine months rather than twelve.
This change will make it more competitive with similar programs and will appeal to working professionals and active duty service members who have to balance professional expectations with academic pursuits.

Students will be able to complete the certificate more quickly, which will both limit their time in the program and allow them to apply the new skills they gain to the workforce more quickly.
Second, the courses

2 Updated: 9.2018 associated with the NRE certificate will be more consistent with URI Online standard practices.
As a result, it will be easier for courses associated with the NRE program to support other online programs currently under development.
To facilitate this role we are also proposing to adjust the pre-requisite language for each remaining NRE course to include enrollment in the NRE certificate or permission of the instructor.
For example, the new Online GIS and Geospatial Technology Certificate is proposing to use the 3-credit version of EVS 509 as a core course and the Online Masters in Oceanography (currently in development) would allow students to take NRE courses to fulfill elective requirements.
Long-term, we anticipate students being able to fulfill the majority of MESM degree requirements by completing online certificates in related areas; updating the structure of the NRE program and courses will provide students the flexibility they need to use NRE courses for this purpose.
We propose to increase the number of credits from two to three for EVS 509, EVS 514, EVS 518 and EVS 519 while eliminating EVS 511 and EVS 515 (Table 1).

Content from EVS 511 will be distributed across EVS 509 and EVS 519 while content from EVS 515 will be added to EVS 514 and EVS 518 (Attachment 1).
As a result, EVS 509 will be a required prerequisite for EVS 519 and EVS 514 will be required for EVS 518.
EVS 509 and 511 were going to use different GIS software, so there was a lot of conceptual redundancy teaching students how to complete the same tasks in different programs.
We will use a different software in EVS 509 that retains the initial functionality required for 509 and adds the spatial analysis tools required for EVS 511 thereby retaining all content and eliminating unnecessary redundancy.
We will restructure EVS 514 to integrate the data visualization concepts throughout and shift several EVS 515 topics into the openings.
We will also add EVS 515 topics to EVS 518 to cover methods associated with the scientific papers being read.
